div.head: II Cn 84.1
div.ab: Eallum us is mycel þearf, þæt we God lufian ⁊ Godes lage fylgean ⁊ godcundan lareowan geornlice hyran.
Eallum us his michel þearf, þæt we Godd lufian ⁊ Godes laga fylgean ⁊ godcundan larewan geornlice hyram ⁊ Godes lage fylgean.
Omnibus nobis magnum opus est, ut Deum uere diligamus et Dei legi seruiamus, sanctis doctoribus deuote pareamus;
Eallum us is mycel ðearf þæt we God lufian ⁊ Godes lage fylian ⁊ godcundan lareowan geor[n]lice hyran.
Eallum us is mycel þearf þæt we God lufian and Godes lage fylgean and godcundan lareowan geornlice hyran.
Uns allen ist starke Noth, dass wir Gott lieben und Gottes Gesetz(e?) befolgen und geistlichen Lehrern eifrig gehorchen.
There is great need for all of us that we love God and follow God's law(s?) and eagerly obey spiritual teachers.
There is great need for us all to love God and to follow God's law, and zealously to obey our spiritual teachers.
There is a great need for all of us to praise God and follow God’s law and zealously heed our spiritual teachers.
div.note: Liebermann would strike A's final ‘⁊ Godes lage fylgean’ as a repetition.
hyran: A adds and Godes lage fylgean
